newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-RAPIDS MOVE INTO FIRST PLACE DESPITE LOSING RECORD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RAPIDS MOVE INTO FIRST PLACE DESPITE LOSING RECORD.

text.p: Despite sporting a losing record, the Colorado Rapids moved into first place in the Western Conference by holding the Tampa Bay Mutiny to one shot in its 2-0 victory in weekend action in Major League Soccer.
Former U.S. international defender Steve Trittschuh and Uruguayan Adrian Paz scored for the Rapids, who improved to 3-5 with nine points.
The Rapids, who have three regulation wins, climbed past the Dallas Burn (4-4, eight points) and the Kansas City Wizards (3-3, seven), who have two relegation victories each.
The Mutiny fell to 4-2 as Rapids goalkeeper Marcus Hahnemann recorded his second shutout in three starts.
Eastern Conference leader D.C. United (5-2) split its games, dropping a 3-2 shootout decision at Dallas Sunday after recording a 2-0 home victory over the Los Angeles Galaxy (1-6) on Friday.
In Sunday's game, goalkeeper Mark Dodd made three saves in the tie-breaker, won by the Burn, 3-2. Teammates Peter Hattrup, Tom Soehn and Ted Eck converted their shootout attempts.
United defender Jeff Agoos scored for both sides in the first half, including an own goal for Dallas. Jason Kreis also had a goal for the Burn.

Bolivian Jaime Moreno, who leads the league with seven goals, forced the shootout in the 88th minute, scoring in his sixth consecutive match to tie a league record set last season by Tampa Bay's Roy Lassiter.
Nidal Baba produced the earliest goal in the MLS' brief history, scoring 26 seconds into the New England Revolution's 2-1 victory over the Wizards in Foxboro.

Chinquinho Conde added a goal for the Revolution (4-2). Preki converted a penalty kick for the Wizards after former Italian international goalkeeper Walter Zenga tripped Zimbabwean Digital Takawira in the penalty area.

In San Jose, former U.S. National Team defender Brian Bliss and South African international Doctor Khumalo scored their first goals of the season for the Columbus Crew (4-2), who recorded a 3-1 road win over the Clash (3-4).
Brian McBride added an insurance goal, while Shawn Medved tallied for the Clash.
In a battle of last-place teams, the New York/New Jersey MetroStars (3-4) edged the visiting Galaxy in a shootout, 1-0.
Former U.S. World Cup captain and goalkeeper Tony Meola made three saves in the shootout. Venezuelan international Giovanni Savarese and John DeBrito converted their attempts.
